clue.text: Picnic area ruined with exceptional rain falling? It can make you sick

indicators.note: something ruined is knocked out of shape, so the remaining letters are rearranged
things that fall drop away, so the letters named here are taken out of the fodder

parts.note: taken as written
the four letters of rain, 'exceptional' meaning they come out in any order rather than as a run

explanation.surface: A picnic spot spoilt by a freak downpour, and the thought of it is enough to turn your stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: Strike R, A, I and N from PICNICAREA, leaving PCICEA, then rearrange those six letters into IPECAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Ipecac is a plant-root syrup long used as an emetic to induce vomiting.

clue.text: Chum (boy) one accompanying a knight in classical style

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase standing for an adjective: a Palladian building is one in classical style

parts.note: a chum is a pal
a boy is a lad
Roman numeral one
taken as written
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A boy and his mate trail after a knight, done up in classical fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: N for knight comes from chess notation, where K is already taken by the king.
explanation.definitionFit: Palladian architecture follows Andrea Palladio's revival of ancient Roman temple forms, the classical style.

clue.text: Collect and organise copper to meet judge and minister

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
to rate something is to judge it

explanation.surface: A police officer, a judge and a clergyman are rounded up together.
explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions with wordplay between them: the verb sense (as a museum curator does) and the noun sense, an assistant clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: To curate is to select and arrange items for display; a curate is an assistant parish priest, a minister of the church.

clue.text: Like a famous orator (Conservative), sarcastic about church

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for Conservative

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for sarcastic wraps around the church

parts.note: sarcastic remarks are ironic
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A Tory speaker, all biting sarcasm about the church, is compared to a great rhetorician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' wraps the sarcastic word around the church, not the Conservative; CE is the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Cicero was the most celebrated orator of ancient Rome, so Ciceronic describes his eloquent manner.

clue.text: Flower masking very soft body part

indicators.note: a mask covers something, so the river surrounds the musical marking

parts.note: a flower in crosswords is something that flows, a river
pianissimo, the musical marking for very soft

explanation.surface: A bloom hides a part of the body that is delicate to the touch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' reads as a bloom but is a river, the Nile, which wraps around PP.
explanation.definitionFit: A nipple is a part of the body, the small projection on the breast.

clue.text: Mounting wickedness before a new month

indicators.note: in a down answer, mounting means climbing upwards, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: sin is wickedness
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Wrongdoing builds up ahead of the turn of a new month.
explanation.walkthrough: SIN read upwards gives NIS, followed by A and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Nisan is the first month of the Jewish religious calendar, when Passover falls.

clue.text: Football team left with final message

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
vale is Latin for farewell, a last word of parting

explanation.surface: A football club departs, leaving a parting note.
explanation.walkthrough: Port Vale is an English football club based in Stoke-on-Trent.
explanation.definitionFit: Port Vale is the name of a professional English football club, so it is an example of a team.

clue.text: See human being half cut, one walking in a certain way

definitions.text: one walking in a certain way

indicators.note: cutting something in half removes one of its halves, so only part of the word stays

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
a human being is a person

explanation.surface: Look at someone who is half drunk, walking in an odd way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half cut' is British slang for tipsy, which suits the lurching walker, but here it simply halves PERSON to PER.
explanation.definitionFit: A loper is someone who moves with a long, easy, bounding stride.

clue.text: Unadorned crusading king? Hard to miss warrior's belt

parts.note: bald means plain, unadorned

indicators.note: missing something means going without it, so the named letters are left out

parts.note: Richard the Lionheart, King of England, led the Third Crusade
taken as written

explanation.surface: A plain crusader king, with a hard time of it, lacks his sword-belt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard' is not an adjective here but the very word to remove from the king's name, Richard the Lionheart.
explanation.definitionFit: A baldric is a belt worn over the shoulder and across the body to carry a sword, as soldiers did.

clue.text: Supporters outside hotel with financial inducements

indicators.note: being outside something means surrounding it, so the supporters wrap around the rest

parts.note: backers are supporters
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
and means together with

explanation.surface: Backers loitering outside a hotel come carrying bribes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' looks like a link word but supplies a piece of its own, the word meaning together with.
explanation.definitionFit: A backhander is British slang for a bribe, money slipped under the table.

clue.text: Bands in balls aboard ship

indicators.note: something aboard a vessel is inside it, so the ship's letters enclose the nonsense

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
balls means nonsense, as does tripe

explanation.surface: Musical groups are playing at dances held on a cruise liner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bands in balls' suggests musicians at dances; 'balls' is the slang for rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Stripes are long narrow bands of colour.

clue.text: Be very angry, then frivolous — change for the better?

parts.note: to seethe is to be very angry
light means frivolous, not serious

explanation.surface: Someone swings from fury to frivolity and wonders if that counts as an improvement.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is loose: a sudden conversion or realisation is a change of mind for the better.
explanation.definitionFit: To see the light is to finally understand or be converted, an idiom for a turn for the better.

clue.text: Cathedral staff opposed accepting dean's ultimate authority

parts.note: a cathedral's chapter is its body of clergy

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the word for opposed takes a letter inside it

parts.note: adverse means opposed

indicators.note: ultimate means last, so only the final letter of the word is used

parts.note: the last letter of dean

explanation.surface: The cathedral clergy resist taking the dean's final word as authoritative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opposed' suggests averse, but it is the near-synonym that holds a D; a cathedral chapter is its governing body of clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: Chapter and verse is an idiom for exact, authoritative citation of a source, from Bible references.

clue.text: Show's furniture item about to be disposed of

indicators.note: something disposed of is thrown away, so the abbreviation is dropped from the word

parts.note: a chair is an item of furniture
C is circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A stage show's prop is about to be thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show's' means 'show is'. Hair is the 1960s rock musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair is a famous stage musical, so it is an example of a show.

clue.text: See winter traveller, refreshed, glow and push on

indicators.note: something refreshed is made new, so these letters are worked into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A refreshed winter walker, glowing, presses on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' just points the reader to the definition; 'refreshed' looks like part of the traveller's story but reworks glow and push on.
explanation.definitionFit: A snowplough is a vehicle that travels the roads in winter clearing snow.

clue.text: What hopeful snooker player did — lost form, dramatically?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: played a shot aiming to sink a ball in a pocket

explanation.walkthrough: In snooker, potting a ball is sinking it in a pocket; the idiom for falling to pieces uses the same words.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means deteriorated badly, while literally a snooker player went for a pot, a shot at sinking a ball.

clue.text: Exalting university with acclaim

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for university
to acclaim is to praise, here in the -ing form

explanation.surface: A university is being lauded with great acclaim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Acclaim' must be read as the participle praising, to match the -ing of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To upraise is an old word for raising up or glorifying, so upraising means exalting.

clue.text: In haste, struggling with a muscular problem

indicators.note: struggling suggests thrashing about out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone in a hurry is battling a muscle complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Asthenia is the medical term for abnormal physical weakness, a loss of muscle strength.

clue.text: Frolicking can end soon — there's very little time

indicators.note: frolicking means romping about playfully, so these letters scamper into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Fun and games must end shortly, as there's little time left.
explanation.definitionFit: A nanosecond is a billionth of a second, a tiny span of time.

clue.text: Exam in which a learner gets nothing right to start with

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
R is the abbreviation for right
taken as written
L is the learner plate on British cars

explanation.surface: A test in which a student scores nothing correct at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To start with' places O and R before A and L.
explanation.definitionFit: An oral is a spoken examination, as in a language test.

clue.text: Bird's eggs sat on by male

parts.note: a gent is a man
O resembles an egg, so two of them are eggs

explanation.surface: A bird's eggs are being incubated by the father.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'sat on' places GENT above OO; male penguins do incubate the eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: The gentoo is a species of penguin, so it is a kind of bird.

clue.text: Very significant hater may emerge thus

parts.note: surface reading: someone who hates might come out of an event in this way
setter's reading: break the first word of the answer apart and its letters can rearrange into hater

explanation.surface: Something momentous happens, and the result is a person consumed by hatred.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse anagram: the answer itself is the instruction, the first word shattered, and doing that to EARTH lets HATER emerge.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth-shattering means momentous, important enough to shake the world.

clue.text: Minister not right but is on the right side!

indicators.note: not signals going without, so the letter for right is removed from the word

parts.note: a rector is a parish minister
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A clergyman who is not in the right is nonetheless on the right side, a paradox.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark points up the apparent contradiction of losing right yet being on the right.
explanation.definitionFit: Recto is the right-hand page of an open book, the front of a leaf.

clue.text: House companion storing old drink

indicators.note: a store holds things inside it, so these letters enclose another

parts.note: HO is the abbreviation for house
CH is Companion of Honour, a British order
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A housemate is keeping old booze hidden away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House companion' reads as one housemate but is two abbreviations, with Companion of Honour a British award.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooch is slang for alcoholic drink, especially cheap or illicitly made liquor.

clue.text: Musical part that oboe has, but not violin

wordplay.note: oboe has two of the round letter and violin only one, so what oboe has and violin lacks is a second one

explanation.surface: An orchestral part is written for the oboe and left out of the violin's music.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters are read as two words, 'second O': count the round letters in each instrument's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Secondo is the lower part in a piano duet, the second player's part.

clue.text: Threesome laid into Irishman, defender of country's honour

indicators.note: laid into means placed inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: Pat is a stock Irish name
a threesome is a trio

explanation.surface: Three people set upon an Irishman who stands up for his nation's good name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laid into' reads as attacked; here it means put inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A patriot is a person who loves and defends their country.

clue.text: Chemical drugs containing poisonous element

indicators.note: containing means holding within, so the drugs surround the element

parts.note: pot (cannabis) and H (heroin) are two drugs
As is the symbol for arsenic

explanation.surface: A stash of narcotics laced with something toxic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drugs' is plural and supplies two: cannabis and heroin.
explanation.definitionFit: Potash is a potassium compound, a chemical used in fertilisers.

clue.text: Hard on the outside, hard on the inside nevertheless

indicators.note: on the outside means forming the shell, so this word wraps around the other
on the inside means placed within, so the abbreviation sits inside the word

parts.note: tough means hard
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Tough outside, tough inside, all the same.
explanation.walkthrough: H goes after the T of TOUGH.
explanation.definitionFit: Though as an adverb means however or nevertheless, as in 'it rained, though'.
